instrument: Legislative Decree No. 96 of 7 May 2026 (Gazzetta Ufficiale No. 125, 1 June 2026), in force 7 June 2026
reporting: Thresholds, frequencies and first deadlines as in Article 9(2)-(4) of the Directive (art. 9(8)-(9)). The gaps, quartile bands and the 5% test are computed on livello retributivo, fixed and continuing pay, not on total pay (art. 3(1)(b), art. 10(1)(a))
notes: Applying a national collective agreement signed by the most representative unions is presumed to comply, classification included; its levels are the reference for work of equal value and an employer's own gender-neutral system may complement them (art. 4). Monitoring body at the Ministry of Labour (art. 14). Implementing decrees on data collection were due within 90 days of 7 June 2026 [to verify whether adopted]
sources: Gazzetta Ufficiale No. 125, 1 June 2026 (text read 24 October 2026); Littler; Cocuzza & Associati; PwC Italia; Lockton implementation tracker

instrument: Labour Code amendment on transparency in recruitment, in force since December 2025; draft act on pay reporting and the right to information published 29 April 2026
reporting: Draft: 250+ every year, 100-249 every three years; first reports 7 June 2027 (150+) and 7 June 2031 (100-149); later reports due by 31 March
notes: Sources give 23 or 24 December 2025 for the recruitment rules. The draft enters into force six months after publication, so Poland missed 7 June 2026. Lockton's tracker (status at 23 September 2026) dates the revised draft 4 May 2026; not adopted by then
sources: DLA Piper GENIE, 18 May 2026; Garrigues; IBA note on Polish recruitment transparency; Lockton implementation tracker, 25 September 2026
